The edges of a cube decrease at a rate of $4\text{ cm/s}.$ At what rate is the volume decreasing when the length of each edge is $26\text{ cm}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the cube and let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\text{ cm/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}$ when $x=26\text{ cm}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the cube:

$$
V={x}^{3}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug $x=26$ and $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\text{ cm/s}$ into the expression for $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3(26)^{2}\cdot (-4)\, \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =-8\,112.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the cube is decreasing at a rate of $8\,112\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s}$ at the moment when $x=26\,\text{cm}.$
